messages:
maria_sre: Heads-up — prepping on-prem deploy checklist for customer X. They require isolation proof, per-tenant KMS, and detailed audit logs forwarded to their SIEM. Two quick asks: 1) preferred KMS integration pattern for key-per-tenant and rotation in air-gapped setup? 2) minimal RBAC changes we can apply without breaking node provisioning. Any past playbooks?

chetan_sec: For KMS in air-gapped: recommend customer-managed HSM + Vault cluster with HSM plugin. Pattern: local Vault (HSM) -> wrap/unwrap keys -> key alias per-tenant. Rotation: 90d rolling with dual-key overlap. Never export private material.

olivia_priv: +1. Also ensure audit logs are signed and forwarded via a syslog-relay VM with TLS and signed delivery receipts. Keep an append-only per-tenant ledger and mirror to S3-compatible store for retention and e-discovery.

ryan_infra: On RBAC: lock kubelet and node-level SA to kube-system roles only, remove cluster-admin from provisioning SA. Use a scoped bootstrap token and a controller that mints ephemeral certs for node agents. Roll changes via canary namespace before cluster-wide.

sam_triage: there's also the container vuln (CVE-2025-1234) hitting our base image. Short-term: rebuild images with patched base, enable image scanning in CI, and block old images via admission controller (Gatekeeper/OPA).

maria_sre: sounds good. For network isolation: customer wants proof of no egress to internet except their approved registry. Proposals?

ryan_infra: Suggest combine deny-by-default NetworkPolicy + egress gateway VM. Minimal netpol to start:

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-default
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```

Then allow specific egress from an egress-gw pod and force all image pulls through it.

chetan_sec: Also recommend mTLS service mesh for pod-to-pod auth and short-lived certs via cert-manager (internal CA). Enforce L7 policies in the mesh for zero-trust.

olivia_priv: For compliance artifacts capture: attestation bundle (SBOM, signature, image digest), RBAC diff, netpol manifest, and a signed audit log snippet showing denied egress attempts. That's what auditors expect.

attest-bot: image-attest(report) — IMAGE: registry.redwood/custx/api:v2.3.4 — SBOM: present — SIGNATURE: pass — POLICY: vuln scan FAIL (1 HIGH). See /artifacts/1857654321/attest/report.json

sam_triage: I'll pick up vuln triage. Short-term plan: patch + rebuild + block old tag via OPA. Long-term: move to minimal base images and reproducible builds.

maria_sre: Incident response question: if we detect image compromise, what's our standard playbook? steps we should share with customer.

chetan_sec: IR playbook (short): 1) Quarantine affected nodes (cordon + drain) 2) Revoke bootstrap/agent tokens 3) Revoke/wrap KMS keys and issue new wrapping keys 4) Blacklist image digests in admission controller 5) Rotate service credentials and audit-forwarder certs 6) Collect forensic artifacts: disk image, running processes, and audit ledger snapshot, hand to IR team.

ryan_infra: Add: temporarily update network policies to block registry pulls for all namespaces except a locked 'release' namespace until rebuilt images verified.

olivia_priv: I'll draft an evidence template: checklist + signed attestations + timeline + CVE remediation notes + RBAC diff. We should include cryptographic hashes of artifacts.

maria_sre: Great. Can someone drop a minimal RBAC diff and netpol example we can share with SOC? Prefer non-breaking defaults.

ryan_infra: pushed quick diff to repo: github.com/redwood-inference/internal/sec-playbooks/patches/1857654321 — includes canary serviceaccount change and the deny-egress netpol.

sam_triage: assigning to @sam_triage to do the rebuild and OPA rule. ETA ~6h.

maria_sre: thanks all. I'll bundle artifacts and send to customer. :thumbsup:
